conventions.convention: The state set is finite and nonempty; T ≥ 0; off-diagonal rates are bounded continuous nonnegative functions. Paths take the new state at a jump. Q has off-diagonal entries κxy and diagonal entries −λx.
Undesignated time integrals are oriented Riemann integrals; jump-time densities use Lebesgue measure under Countable Choice. Empty products equal 1, and T = 0 permits only the no-jump case.
Probability distributions are row vectors and obey p′ = pQ; a common stationary vector satisfies πQ(t) = 0 at every time.

Stationary entropy uses natural logarithms of πx qxy/(πy qyx), with strictly positive stationary π and symmetric rate support. Its no-jump value and its value on the exceptional null complement are zero. It is dimensionless and has no automatic thermodynamic interpretation.
The fluctuation relation is an equality of measures for every Borel set, without assuming an entropy density.

Work is the time integral of the state-energy derivative, β > 0, and ΔF = −β⁻¹ log(ZT/Z0). The process starts in π0 and satisfies instantaneous detailed balance; no irreducibility or thermalization hypothesis is imposed.
The ring has N ≥ 3, clockwise rate a > 0, counterclockwise rate b > 0, and uniform initial law; these two destination states are distinct.

load_bearing.statement: For bounded continuous finite-state rates, each finite path has density ρ(x0) times the product of its jump rates times exp(−Σj ∫[tj,tj+1] λxj(s) ds). For Mδ < 1, P(NJ ≥ n) ≤ (Mδ)^n and E[NJ] ≤ Mδ/(1−Mδ). The total jump count on every finite horizon has finite expectation, so the process is nonexplosive.
Conditional on the history through time s and Xs = x, next-jump survival is Hx(s,t) = exp(−∫sᵗ λx(u) du), the next-jump density to y ≠ x is Hx(s,t)κxy(t), and this rule restarts after each jump.

For bounded continuous finite-state rates, the marginal row vector satisfies p′(t) = p(t)Q(t), with one-sided endpoint derivatives when T > 0. If πQ(t) = 0 for every t and p(0) = π, then p(t) = π throughout [0,T]. At T = 0 only the initial marginal is asserted.

For continuous potentials Vx, the weighted endpoint masses Gy(t) = E[exp(−∫0ᵗ VXs(s) ds) 1{Xt=y}] uniquely solve Gy′ = Σx≠y Gxκxy − Gyλy − VyGy with G(0) = ρ; at T = 0 only the singleton initial value is asserted.

For a finite irreducible time-homogeneous chain with symmetric rate support, strictly positive stationary law π, and initial law π, P(ST ∈ B) = ∫−B e⁻ᵘ μT(du) for every Borel B; E[e⁻ˢᵀ] = 1 and E[ST] ≥ 0.
For distinct states x,y of a finite-state process with bounded continuous rates, E[Nxy(T)] = ∫0ᵀ px(t)κxy(t) dt. The integral is finite; no stationarity assumption is required.

concerns.concern: F4 attributes to thm-ftc-first-part: “for a continuous derivative a′ on [0,T], ∫0ᵀ a′(t) dt = a(T)−a(0).” The opened supplier states that the derivative of an integral function equals its integrand; it does not state this integral-of-a-derivative conclusion. Step 4.1 uses the stronger restatement. The conclusion is valid for the stated C1 shift, but needs the second FTC or the short first-FTC plus zero-derivative argument with its prerequisite.
